title: Cohomology of a coherent module with zero-dimensional support

source.place: Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite), parts (3), (4) and (5) with $\mathcal E$ invertible ($n=1$)

proof.text: Because $X$ is proper over the field $k$, it is of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The support of a coherent module is closed, and its dimension is at most zero by hypothesis; therefore [lem-sc-dim0-finite] shows that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is a finite set of closed points.

source.place: Tag 0AYT, proof of parts (3)--(5): a coherent module with zero-dimensional support has finite support

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-zero-support-finite-scheme] to obtain $A$, $i:\operatorname{Spec}(A)\hookrightarrow X$, and $\mathcal G$. The displayed cohomology identifications there reduce both $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N$ to coherent modules on the affine finite scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, with $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N$ coherent and having the same support as $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Tag 0AYT, proof: replace the sheaf by its module on the finite closed subscheme cut out by its annihilator

proof.text: The algebra $A$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, so [lem-pc-finite-scheme-cohomology-tensor] gives vanishing of all positive-degree cohomology, finite-dimensional global sections, and equality of the dimensions of the global sections before and after tensoring by $i^*\mathcal N$. Transporting these facts through the cohomology identifications of the previous step gives $H^q(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for $q>0$ and $H^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N)=0$ for $q>0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYT, parts (3) and (4): higher cohomology vanishes on the finite support and the tensor remains coherent

proof.text: By the definition of Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic], the vanishing in the preceding step gives $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N)$. The global-section identifications in [lem-pc-zero-support-finite-scheme] and the dimension equality in [lem-pc-finite-scheme-cohomology-tensor] identify these two dimensions, so $\chi(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N)=\chi(X,\mathcal F)$.
